extracted.intended_audience: labor policymakers, employers, unions, and general newspaper readers
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting of procedural standards and substantive criteria used by fact‑finding/wage panels (and related Labor Department actions) to evaluate and recommend wage increases, conditions for panels, and limits when price relief may be implicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel recommendation bases (2(A) and 2(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel may recommend a wage increase on either of two bases: (A) that the wage increase recommended is one which can be paid without any increase in existing price ceilings or in costs to the United States; or (B) that the wage increase recommended is, in its judgment, approvable under Executive Order 9651 and the wage and salary regulations of the Stabilization Administrator — i.e., an increase of a type which may be used as a basis for an increase in price ceilings or costs to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mutually exclusive bases for recommendations: A focuses on absorbability without price relief; B contemplates increases that could justify price relief under the Executive Order and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for immediate-effect recommendations under 2(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the panel recommends a wage increase under 2(A), it may, without reference to governmental stabilization agencies, recommend that the employer put it into effect immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance of such a recommendation by an employer will amount to a waiver of any right to use the wage increase within a six-month period as a basis for seeking price relief so long as the increase has not been approved by the Wage Stabilization Board. An employer may, however, after putting the wage increase into effect, still seek approval from the Wage Stabilization Board; if approval were later given the employer could then use that approval as a basis for seeking price relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to satisfy panel of employer's ability to absorb increase (ability-to-pay limitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the panel recommends an increase under 2(A) (i.e., one intended to be absorbed without price ceiling increases), it must satisfy itself that the employers are in a position to absorb the whole increase without any increase in price ceilings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to pay is a limitation on recommending increases and does not necessarily constitute a measure of the amount of a fair increase. The panel should not recommend an increase which it believes will require the employer after six months to obtain price relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples limiting recommended amounts (numeric comparators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel should limit recommendations to amounts it finds can be absorbed; it cannot properly recommend an amount larger than the maximum it finds absorbable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from text: if panel finds a 10-cent/hour increase could be absorbed without price ceilings rising, and a 5-cent increase would be approvable under Exec. Order 9651, the panel may recommend a 10-cent increase but cannot properly recommend a 15-cent increase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of inquiry for ability-to-pay (profits, earnings, costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary to satisfy itself that employers can absorb a recommended increase without price increases, the panel is to inquire into the profits and earnings position of the employer, and may also inquire into production and other costs and other data bearing on ability to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel may use company evidence, union evidence, or evidence it secures itself; it may draw inferences from failure to produce evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence standard and inference when employer does not contest inability
rubrics_metrics.description: If employers do not contend that there is an inability to pay the requested wage increase, the panel still must satisfy itself on the basis of evidence satisfactory to it whether any increase it recommends is absorbable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel is free to draw such inferences as it chooses from an employer’s failure to produce evidence. It may take union evidence and other evidence it secures, or rely on the company's failure to contest the issue as an establishment of ability to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPA pricing standards advisory, not controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: In any inquiry into ability to pay, the panel should not be guided solely by the OPA’s standards for authorizing price increases as a test of ability to pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPA pricing standards were devised for a different purpose and may throw light on an employer’s ability to pay a wage increase under existing price ceilings, but they should not be used as a controlling test. The OPA standards generally measure need for price increases by comparing current earnings with prewar/peacetime earnings; those metrics may be misleading in some industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on recommendations involving price relief and approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any increase that may be recommended by the panel which is to be used as a basis for seeking price relief must receive the approval of the Wage Stabilization Board and is limited to an increase not in excess of the amount approvable for price purposes by the Wage Stabilization Board or other designated wage or salary stabilization agency under the standards laid down in Executive Order 9651 and the wage and salary regulations of the Stabilization Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel has two alternatives: (A) secure informal advice through the Secretary’s office about approvability, or (B) condition its recommendation upon approval by the Wage Stabilization Board. If the panel limits its recommendation to a wage increase appropriate for price purposes, it may (but is not required to) recommend up to the limit approvable under Exec. Order 9651 criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel may recommend policy changes if pricing criteria inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the panel believes that the standards for allowing price increases should be broadened, it is free to suggest to the Stabilization Administrator, through the Secretary of Labor, that he consider taking action in accordance with Section 302(B) of the wage and salary stabilization regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel would conform its final findings and recommendations with any action taken by the Stabilization Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary-imposed prerequisites for establishing fact-finding panels (Greyhound example)
rubrics_metrics.description: When appointing fact-finding panels, the Secretary of Labor may impose conditions as prerequisites to establishment — e.g., in the Greyhound dispute the Secretary asked for an immediate end of the strike, that any pay increases be retroactive to Oct. 31, and that the company reinstate strikers without penalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies may accept some but not all conditions; refusal of conditions (such as retroactivity) may impede or delay fact-finding or settlement efforts.
